title: Linear App Pricing: Every Plan and Seat Cost (2026)
summary: Linear app pricing is per-member based, with Business at $16 per seat, so you can calculate your team's total monthly bill.
body_markdown:
## Compare Linear's price against Jira, Shortcut, ClickUp, Asana


Linear's per-seat price rarely separates it from Jira, Shortcut, ClickUp or[Asana](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/asana) .


What does is which plan holds single sign-on (one company login for every tool) and advanced reporting, and how soon the free tier runs out. That's also why a seat you can remove without a credit matters so much.


### Price and limits side by side


I have no vendor-verified figures to put in a table here, and a comparison built on remembered prices would be worse than none.


Pull the free-tier limits, the entry paid price, the single sign-on tier and the reporting tier from each vendor's own pricing page. Write down the date you checked, because all five change their plans.


Doing nothing costs you here. If you compare only the headline per-seat price, you'll pick the tool that looks cheapest and find out at renewal that login control or reporting sits one plan higher.


### Where Linear costs more or less


If your whole team writes and ships code, Linear suits you: it is built for software teams and keeps its plan structure fairly simple, so there are fewer places for a surprise.


It hurts if you add people who only need to look. Designers, support staff and managers each count as a seat unless the plan says otherwise, so ask each vendor how it treats occasional users.


Jira, ClickUp and Asana are broader tools, so a mixed team can cost less on one of them even when the engineering seats cost more.


### When Jira, Asana or Shortcut beats Linear


Pick on the work, then check the price. Jira suits teams that need heavy configuration and approval rules.


Asana and ClickUp suit teams where most users aren't engineers. Shortcut is the closest in spirit to Linear, so compare the two on the plan you'll actually need.


Choose Linear when speed and a focused workflow matter more than flexibility, and when the seat count you price is the one you'll have next year.
